mermaid:
graph TB
    %% Styles and classes
    classDef jsLayer fill:#a8d1f0,stroke:#333
    classDef nativeLayer fill:#90EE90,stroke:#333
    classDef bridge fill:#FFB347,stroke:#333
    classDef devTools fill:#DDA0DD,stroke:#333

    %% Legend
    subgraph Legend
        JS[JavaScript Layer]:::jsLayer
        NTV[Native Layer]:::nativeLayer
        BRG[Bridge Layer]:::bridge
        DEV[Development Tools]:::devTools
    end

    %% Application Layer
    subgraph ApplicationLayer
        ReactCore["React Core (JavaScript)"]:::jsLayer
        VirtualDOM["Virtual DOM"]:::jsLayer
        Components["React Components"]:::jsLayer
        StateManagement["State Management"]:::jsLayer
    end

    %% Framework Layer
    subgraph FrameworkLayer
        %% Bridge Components
        Bridge["Native Module Bridge"]:::bridge
        EventSystem["Event System"]:::bridge
        ModuleRegistry["Native Module Registry"]:::bridge
        
        %% Core Components
        ReactInstance["React Instance Manager"]:::jsLayer
        UIManager["UI Manager"]:::jsLayer
        Renderer["Renderer"]:::jsLayer
        
        %% JavaScript Engine
        Hermes["Hermes JS Engine"]:::jsLayer
    end

    %% Platform Layer
    subgraph PlatformLayer
        %% iOS
        subgraph iOSPlatform
            iOSComponents["iOS Components (UIKit)"]:::nativeLayer
            iOSModules["iOS Native Modules"]:::nativeLayer
        end
        
        %% Android
        subgraph AndroidPlatform
            AndroidComponents["Android Components (SDK)"]:::nativeLayer
            AndroidModules["Android Native Modules"]:::nativeLayer
        end
    end

    %% Development Tools
    subgraph DevTools
        MetroBundler["Metro Bundler"]:::devTools
        DevMenu["Developer Menu"]:::devTools
        HotReload["Hot Reloading"]:::devTools
        DebugInfra["Debug Infrastructure"]:::devTools
    end

    %% Relationships
    ReactCore --> VirtualDOM
    VirtualDOM --> Components
    Components --> StateManagement
    Components --> Bridge
    Bridge --> ModuleRegistry
    ModuleRegistry --> iOSModules
    ModuleRegistry --> AndroidModules
    Bridge --> EventSystem
    EventSystem --> ReactInstance
    ReactInstance --> UIManager
    UIManager --> Renderer
    Renderer --> iOSComponents
    Renderer --> AndroidComponents
    Bridge --> Hermes

    %% Development Tool Connections
    MetroBundler -.-> ReactCore
    DevMenu -.-> ReactInstance
    HotReload -.-> Components
    DebugInfra -.-> Bridge

    %% Click Events
    click Bridge "https://github.com/facebook/react-native/tree/main/packages/react-native/ReactCommon/react/bridge/"
    click Hermes "https://github.com/facebook/react-native/blob/main/packages/react-native/ReactCommon/hermes/executor/HermesExecutorFactory.cpp"
    click UIManager "https://github.com/facebook/react-native/blob/main/packages/react-native/ReactCommon/react/renderer/uimanager/UIManager.h"
    click EventSystem "https://github.com/facebook/react-native/blob/main/packages/react-native/ReactCommon/react/renderer/events/EventEmitter.h"
    click ReactInstance "https://github.com/facebook/react-native/blob/main/packages/react-native/ReactAndroid/src/main/java/com/facebook/react/ReactInstanceManager.java"
    click iOSComponents "https://github.com/facebook/react-native/tree/main/packages/react-native/React/Base/"
    click AndroidComponents "https://github.com/facebook/react-native/tree/main/packages/react-native/ReactAndroid/src/main/java/com/facebook/react/"
    click Renderer "https://github.com/facebook/react-native/tree/main/packages/react-native/ReactCommon/react/renderer/core/"
    click DebugInfra "https://github.com/facebook/react-native/tree/main/packages/react-native/ReactCommon/react/debug/"
    click Components "https://github.com/facebook/react-native/tree/main/packages/react-native/Libraries/Components/"

Here's my explanation for creating a system design diagram for React Native based on the provided file tree and README:

<explanation>
To create an accurate system design diagram for React Native, I recommend focusing on the following key architectural components and their relationships:

1. Core Components & Architecture

a. Main Building Blocks:
- React Core (JavaScript)
- Native Modules Bridge
- Platform-specific Native Code (iOS/Android)
- JavaScript Engine (Hermes)

b. Key Components to Highlight:
- ReactInstanceManager
- UIManager
- Native Modules
- JavaScript Runtime
- Event System
- Renderer

2. Data Flow & Communication

Draw bidirectional arrows showing:
- JavaScript to Native Bridge communication
- Event propagation
- State management
- UI updates

3. Major Subsystems

Group and represent the following subsystems:

a. JavaScript Core:
- React Components
- Virtual DOM
- Component Lifecycle
- State Management

b. Bridge Layer:
- Native Module Registry
- Method Invocation
- Event Emitter
- Serialization/Deserialization

c. Native Platforms:
- iOS Components (UIKit)
- Android Components (Android SDK)
- Native Modules
- Platform APIs

d. Development Tools:
- Metro Bundler
- Developer Menu
- Hot Reloading
- Debugging Infrastructure

4. Key Interactions

Show the following flows:
- Component Rendering Pipeline
- Event Handling
- Native Module Calls
- Bridge Communication
- State Updates

5. Supporting Infrastructure

Include:
- Build System
- Package Management
- Development Server
- Testing Infrastructure

Visual Representation Guidelines:

1. Use distinct colors for:
- JavaScript layer (e.g., blue)
- Native layer (e.g., green)
- Bridge components (e.g., orange)
- Development tools (e.g., purple)

2. Use different shapes for:
- Core components (rectangles)
- Services (hexagons)
- Data stores (cylinders)
- External interfaces (clouds)

3. Connection Types:
- Solid lines for direct communication
- Dashed lines for async operations
- Double lines for data flow
- Dotted lines for development-time connections

4. Include a Legend:
- Component types
- Connection types
- Color coding
- Important symbols

5. Layer Organization:
- Application Layer (top)
- Framework Layer (middle)
- Platform Layer (bottom)

Additional Considerations:

1. Performance Critical Paths:
- Highlight render cycle
- Event propagation
- Bridge communication

2. Development Workflow:
- Show how code changes flow
- Indicate hot reload paths
- Debug information flow

3. Error Handling:
- Error boundaries
- Native error propagation
- JavaScript error handling

4. Security Boundaries:
- JavaScript sandbox
- Native code permissions
- Bridge security

5. Scalability Aspects:
- Component reuse
- Code splitting
- Resource management

The diagram should be organized in a top-down manner, with:

1. Top Layer:
- Application code
- React components
- JavaScript business logic

2. Middle Layer:
- React Native framework
- Bridge
- Core modules

3. Bottom Layer:
- Native platform code
- Platform-specific implementations
- Device APIs

Remember to:

1. Keep the diagram clean and readable
2. Use consistent styling
3. Group related components
4. Show clear boundaries between layers
5. Include important subsystems
6. Demonstrate key data flows
7. Highlight critical paths
8. Show extension points

This structure will provide a comprehensive view of the React Native architecture while maintaining clarity and usefulness for a principal software engineer.

</explanation>
